source: Hoek, Practical Rock Engineering, Chapter 11 'Rock mass properties', Table 2: Field estimates of uniaxial compressive strength (grade after Brown 1981). PDF in the suite bibliography (Rocas/Hoek_Practical-Rock-Engineering_Ch11_Rock-Mass-Properties.pdf).
note: Point load index is not reliable below 25 MPa uniaxial strength (note ** of the source table). Open-ended grade R6 uses its printed lower bound (250 MPa) as the pick value. Pick values are the representative values written by the reference program and ORMAS V2.0 (both verified 2026-11-23: 250, 175, 75, 35, 15, 3, 0.6 MPa; 08_estimacion_sin_ensayos.md); they equal the range midpoints except R3 (35) and R0 (0.6).

grades.field_estimate: Specimen can only be chipped with a geological hammer
grades.examples: Fresh basalt, chert, diabase, gneiss, granite, quartzite

grades.field_estimate: Specimen requires many blows of a geological hammer to fracture it
grades.examples: Amphibolite, sandstone, basalt, gabbro, gneiss, granodiorite, limestone, marble, rhyolite, tuff

grades.field_estimate: Specimen requires more than one blow of a geological hammer to fracture it
grades.examples: Limestone, marble, phyllite, sandstone, schist, shale

grades.field_estimate: Cannot be scraped or peeled with a pocket knife, specimen can be fractured with a single blow from a geological hammer
grades.examples: Claystone, coal, concrete, schist, shale, siltstone

grades.field_estimate: Can be peeled with a pocket knife with difficulty, shallow indentation made by firm blow with point of a geological hammer
Crumbles under firm blows with point of a geological hammer, can be peeled by a pocket knife
